entrypoints.review: mach_absolute_time + dispatch_once; no wall clock or new OS time API.
Preserves baseline through reset and rejects unchanged cache generation/age.
Foreign door/origin/owner is rejected before changing the active timing anchor.
Copies and frees real C status JSON on existing serial queue, checks Core generation before and after.
Expected generation is checked on the actual C dispatch queue.
Current snapshot state/origin/door and Core recovery flags control acceptance.
Unknown/zero checks Core again; no inferred cancellation; object and generation token isolate old timer.
Requires persisted targeted identity; uses Core reading and original tracker revision deduplication.
Event selects only identity; snapshot owns state/owner and ten-second recovery validity.
Checks current reading identity/door/revision/duration then retains original terminal and revision dedupe.
Exact call/door/revision with captured Core generation, fixed ten-second TTL and 128 identity cap. Repeated revisions do not renew TTL.
Each identity has its own timing anchor. Only a new snapshot sample can resolve pending admission; expired/unknown time does not activate UI or issue cancellation.
At most one read and one retry timer. Captured Core generation and recovery epoch gate final main delivery; background/foreground requires a fresh sample.
Queues the already targeted Core event and checks current Core remaining duration; NSDate is no longer an admission authority.
Unreachable wall-clock autoClose code was deleted. Existing DBCallReturnCountdown uses its original local return behavior and pauses while a dialog is active.

preserved_outside_scope: DBIncomingScreen actual local return countdown remains unchanged; removed only the unreachable legacy wall-clock autoClose branch
NSDate notice timestamps, media metadata, clock labels and secret admin tap interval are not call timing authority
